title: Health improvements of type 2 diabetic patients through diet and diet plus fecal microbiota transplantation
conclusion: In 8 people with type 2 diabetes, 90 days of a diet supplemented with probiotics, prebiotic fiber and whole grains significantly lowered BMI (24.8 to 23.4), HbA1c (8.3% to 6.6%) and systolic blood pressure (135 to 118 mmHg) compared with baseline. Fasting blood glucose fell sharply during the first 20 days (9.6 to 6.7 mmol/L) and partly rebounded by day 90, while Bifidobacterium increased and the sulfate-reducing bacterium Bilophila decreased.
relevance: Supports the idea that a fiber- and probiotic-rich diet can improve blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes alongside a shift toward bacteria considered beneficial. But it is a very small open-label study with no untreated comparison group, the first 20 days were a supervised hospital stay, and it was funded in part by the company that makes the diet products.

title: Health improvements of type 2 diabetic patients through diet and diet plus fecal microbiota transplantation
conclusion: Adding three weekly rounds of oral FMT capsules to the same diet in 5 people with type 2 diabetes brought earlier weight loss and faster gut microbiome change (toward Prevotella), and HbA1c (6.9% to 5.9%) and systolic blood pressure (133 to 109 mmHg) fell by day 20. However, clinical changes did not differ significantly from the diet-only group, which the authors attribute to the small sample, and HbA1c partly rebounded by day 90.
relevance: An early test of FMT as an add-on to diet for type 2 diabetes: it suggests FMT may speed up microbiome change and soften the diet-related drop in microbial diversity, with no adverse reactions reported, but it shows no added clinical benefit yet. With only 5 FMT patients (3 dropped out) and no placebo, it is best treated as a pilot.
